Metabolic signatures of the peritoneal microenvironment are associated with peritoneal inflammation and with perturbation of glucose metabolism and immunometabolism

Metabolic signatures of the peritoneal microenvironment are associated with peritoneal inflammation and with perturbation of glucose metabolism and immunometabolism. (a) Principal component analysis of metabolic signatures in patients with high versus low peritoneal inflammation. (b) Metabolic pathway enrichment (FDR < 0.01) with significantly changed metabolites (n = 154, P < 0.05, linear mixed-model) in patients with high peritoneal inflammation. (c) Pathway enrichment network of shared metabolites (pathways connected if shared metabolites exceed 25% of the number of their combined metabolite sets); P value: circle color; circle size: fold enrichment ratio (hits/expected). (d) Activation network analysis of highly changed metabolites in the peritoneal microenvironment (n = 136, q < 0.05) with high peritoneal inflammation. (e) Activation network analysis of highly changed metabolites (q < 0.05) in patients with high cell function (high ex vivo–stimulated IL-6 release, stratified at median). (d and e) Oval shape: significantly changed metabolites; green: reduced abundance; red: increased abundance; diamonds: affected proteins; blue: inhibited; violet: activated; orange lines: findings inconsistent with downstream molecule state (per IPA data base). Bile acids: (GCDCA, glycochenodeoxycholic acid), (LCA, lithocholic acid), (TCA, taurocholic acid); CE, cholesterol esters; Cer, ceramides; DHA, dehydroascorbic acid; LPC, lysophosphatidylcholine; PC, phosphatidylcholines; PE. phosphatidylethanolamines; SM, sphingomyelins. (f) Correlation of peritoneal cell function and daily peritoneal glucose exposure (g/d), P = 0.0001, linear mixed-model
